title: Linter adds a hardcoded absolute path to tsconfig

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue was opened via the bug report template.

body:
### Verify canary release

- [X] I verified that the issue exists in the latest Next.js canary release

### Provide environment information


    Operating System:
      Platform: darwin
      Arch: arm64
      Version: Darwin Kernel Version 22.2.0: Fri Nov 11 02:03:51 PST 2022; root:xnu-8792.61.2~4/RELEASE_ARM64_T6000
    Binaries:
      Node: 16.14.0
      npm: 8.3.1
      Yarn: 1.22.17
      pnpm: 7.27.0
    Relevant packages:
      next: 13.2.3-canary.1
      eslint-config-next: 13.2.3
      react: 18.2.0
      react-dom: 18.2.0



### Which area(s) of Next.js are affected? (leave empty if unsure)

CLI (create-next-app), Package manager (npm, pnpm, Yarn), TypeScript

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://codesandbox.io/p/sandbox/keen-chaum-kv9sgw?file=%2Ftsconfig.json&selection=%5B%7B%22endColumn%22%3A29%2C%22endLineNumber%22%3A11%2C%22startColumn%22%3A29%2C%22startLineNumber%22%3A11%7D%5D

### To Reproduce

1. Create a new TS repo using the CLI: `pnpm create next-app --typescript `
2. Either:
	1. Set a custom `distDir` in the `next.config.js` file, e.g. `distDir: '.build;`
	2. Remove the `.next/types/**/*.ts` in the `include` part of `tsconfig.json`
4. Run `pnpm lint`

### Describe the Bug

The linter process detects the new dist dir or the lacking include element and tries to add it. However, the `distDir` that is being used is the absolute path, not the relative and the CLI ends up adding an absolute path to tsconfig, not suited for committing since it's device-specific.

### Expected Behavior

Linting to add the path relatively, not as an absolute path.

PS: Running `pnpm dev` works fine and adds the correct relative path, so the calculation of `distDir` seems to be off for the linter but not for the dev server.
